Publish from SketchUp#

Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — upload core tested, needs a real SketchUp install. The extension's shared Ruby helper published GLB, OBJ (with units) and IFC files, one-shot and resumable, to a real local Verse server; every scene finished and opened; a dead server and a cancel each gave one plain sentence (web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs). The zip writer's output passes Python's zipfile.testzip(). The SketchUp side — menu, exporter options, progress dialog — is written to SketchUp's documented Ruby API but has not been run inside SketchUp yet.

Extensions ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse exports the open model with SketchUp's own exporter, uploads it, shows the server's build stages, and gives you a streaming share link — copied to the clipboard and opened in the browser. Built for architects and real-estate teams who want a client link without leaving SketchUp.

You need: SketchUp 2021 or newer. SketchUp 2025+ exports GLB directly; older versions export OBJ or FBX, which needs SketchUp Pro (Free/Make cannot export them).

1. Install#

Download verse_publish-sketchup-4.0.0-beta.1.rbz from the downloads page once the packages are published, or build it from the repo:

Code
sh integrations/aec/sketchup/make_rbz.sh   # -> integrations/aec/sketchup/dist/verse_publish-sketchup-4.0.0-beta.1.rbz

In SketchUp: Window ▸ Extension Manager ▸ Install Extension, pick the .rbz. No restart needed. A Verse submenu appears under Extensions.

2. Server and key#

Extensions ▸ Verse ▸ Settings… asks for:

FieldWhat it is
Server URLhttps://verse.ctruh.com by default; your own deployment works the same (run your own server)
API keyfor servers that require one
Account tokenfrom Studio — the scene becomes account-owned and you draw from your account's upload limit
Export formatauto (GLB on 2025+, else OBJ), glb, obj or fbx
Open the link when done / Selection only
Use server + key for every Verse plug-insaves them for Revit, Rhino, 3ds Max and Archicad too

Nothing is compiled into the extension. Settings live in one per-user file that every Verse plug-in shares — %APPDATA%\Ctruh\VersePublish\settings.json on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Ctruh/VersePublish/settings.json on macOS — in a sketchup section (or the shared section when you tick "every plug-in"). The file is owner-only on macOS. VERSE_SERVER, VERSE_API_KEY and VERSE_TOKEN in the environment override it.

3. Publish#

  1. Extensions ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse (or the toolbar button).
  2. A progress dialog walks through **exporting → uploading % → building (stage) → done. Cancel** stops it; you are told whether anything reached the server.
  3. The link is shown, copied, and opened when that setting is on.

Success looks like: the dialog ends with the link (also on the clipboard, and opened in the browser); the scene opens on any device at the real size — a 10 m wall measures 10 m.

Files over 100 MB use the resumable upload: a dropped connection resumes where the server got to.

What gets exported#

  • SketchUp 2025+: model.export("….glb") — binary glTF with materials and textures, uploaded as is.
  • Older, or format obj / fbx: SketchUp's exporter with units: "m", Y-up, texture maps on, faces triangulated; the model, its .mtl and texture folder are zipped and the server converts them (Upload FBX and OBJ).
  • Units: SketchUp works in inches internally; the exporter writes metres, so a 10 m wall is 10 m in the link.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at …"Wrong server URL, no internet, or a firewall / proxy blocking the plug-in.Check Server URL in Extensions ▸ Verse ▸ Settings… (default https://verse.ctruh.com) and open it in a browser.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, was revoked, or belongs to another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy the token again from Studio, or clear it to publish without an account.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"This server only takes uploads with an API key; the sentence ends with its reason.Enter the key from the server's operator in Extensions ▸ Verse ▸ Settings….
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the API key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token from Studio (a higher limit).
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"The upload kept failing …"The connection dropped again and again.Publish again when the connection is steady; a large upload continues where it stopped.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."STEP / IGES / native CAD files are not built by the server yet.Export GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that.
"Stopped waiting for the server. The scene is still being built …"You cancelled after the upload; the server keeps building.The scene appears in your Verse dashboard (with an account token) when it is ready.
"SketchUp could not export OBJ. OBJ export needs SketchUp Pro."SketchUp before 2025 has no GLB export, and Free/Make has no OBJ / FBX export.Use SketchUp Pro, or SketchUp 2025+ with Export format: glb.
"There is nothing to publish — the model is empty."No visible geometry (or nothing selected with Selection only).Unhide the model or select it, then publish again.

Anything else: send the whole sentence (and, for a build error, the scene name) to hello@ctruh.com.

What has been tested#

Shared Ruby helper → real server: GLB / OBJ+units / IFC, one-shot + resumable, scene done and opening, dead server, canceltested
Settings file shared with the Python and C# plug-ins (same values read back, env overrides, bad URL refused)tested
ruby -c on every file; .rbz contentstested
Menu, exporter calls, progress dialog, thread pumping inside SketchUpneeds a real install
